questions.question: What does 'contemporary art' generally refer to?
choices: Art made in the present era, including varied practices and perspectives
Only art made before 1800
One fixed visual style
Artwork created exclusively with computers

questions.question: What is an installation artwork?
choices: A framed print only
A work arranged in a space so viewers experience its environment or relationships
A method of painting wet plaster
A sculpture's shipping process

questions.question: What does site-specific art mean?
choices: It can be displayed anywhere without change
It is always a digital image
The work is designed in response to a particular location
It must be smaller than the room

questions.question: Conceptual art often places emphasis on
choices: technical realism only
the cost of materials
the frame's decoration
the idea or concept behind the work

questions.question: A contemporary artwork invites viewers to walk through it. What can this change?
choices: The viewer's physical experience becomes part of encountering the work
The artwork becomes a printed book
The artist loses authorship automatically
The work has no meaning

questions.question: Why might contemporary artists use video, sound, or digital media?
choices: They are required for every contemporary work
These media can address time, technology, movement, or communication
They prevent viewers from interpreting the work
They eliminate the need for ideas

questions.question: What is public art?
choices: Art that has no audience
Art made only in a private studio
Art intended for or placed in spaces accessible to a broader public
Art that cannot include sculpture

questions.question: A community helps design a mural about local history. What is one likely feature of this process?
choices: The mural must be anonymous
Public art cannot use historical themes
Only one person may contribute ideas
Community perspectives can shape the work's subject and meaning

questions.question: Why should a viewer consider who is represented in an artwork?
choices: Representation can shape visibility, identity, and interpretation
It determines the work's exact market price
It proves the artist's intention completely
It removes the need to look closely

questions.question: An artist uses recycled materials to address consumption. What relationship is the work exploring?
choices: A requirement that all art be temporary
Material choice and environmental or social meaning
The history of oil painting only
A color-mixing rule

questions.question: What is an ethical question that may arise in contemporary art?
choices: Whether every artwork must rhyme
Whether the gallery has enough frames
How permissions, cultural ownership, and community impacts are handled
Whether the work uses a title

questions.question: A work changes when viewers contribute messages. What type of participation is involved?
choices: Linear perspective
Fresco painting
Contrapposto
Interactive or participatory engagement

questions.question: Why can an artist's statement help viewers?
choices: It can provide context about questions, materials, or intentions behind the work
It fixes one required interpretation
It replaces the artwork
It proves every viewer must agree

questions.question: What should viewers remember when reading an artist's statement?
choices: It is the only possible meaning
It is useful context, while visual evidence and other interpretations still matter
It replaces historical research
It must be treated as a museum label

questions.question: A contemporary sculpture is temporary and will change outdoors. What concept may be central?
choices: A requirement of classical proportion
A ban on audience response
Time, material change, or impermanence
A fixed permanent surface

questions.question: What is a curatorial choice?
choices: A method for carving marble
A way to calculate perspective
A kind of paint pigment
A decision about selecting and arranging works for an exhibition

questions.question: An exhibition places two works side by side. What can this arrangement do?
choices: Encourage viewers to compare or connect the works
Guarantee they share one meaning
Remove their historical context
Make the works identical

questions.question: Why may contemporary art address social or political questions?
choices: Art is required to endorse one policy
Artists can use visual practice to examine current issues and experiences
Art cannot address public life
Only written essays can discuss society

questions.question: A viewer dislikes an artwork. What is a productive next step for analysis?
choices: Stop looking immediately
Assume the artist failed
Describe the choices that shaped the response and support an interpretation with evidence
Treat personal taste as the only standard

questions.question: Which statement best describes diversity in contemporary art?
choices: All contemporary artists share one message
Only digital works qualify
Contemporary art excludes craft
Artists work across many styles, media, communities, and purposes
